The user rc is read-only to plugin management — the generated loader replaces the managed block (niubash#359 case A, 1.4.2). The control plane (`~/.niubash/plugins.toml` + `~/.niubash/sources/registry.toml`) now drives a derived activation plane: `niu plugin` verbs render and publish `~/.niubash/generated/plugins.niu` (deterministic, byte-stable when the manifest is unchanged, validate-then-atomic-publish so a failed generation never replaces the last good one and a concurrent reader never sees a missing file — the #304 invariant moves to the loader). The host sources that loader BEFORE the us

Double-execution guard for the migration window: the loader generation records the managed-block marker pairs it supersedes; at startup the host scans the rc read-only and keeps the loader OFF while any superseded block still executes (rather than run the plugin set twice), with a one-time hint naming `niu plugin migrate-rc`. Removing the old block by hand — the only removal there has ever been — turns the loader on. `niu doctor` reports the transition state read-only.

New verb `niu plugin migrate-rc [--diff]`: the read-only migration diagnostic. It scans the rc for legacy managed blocks (exact and hand-edited marker shapes, with line ranges and a begin-without-end malformed state reported, never fatal), publishes the candidate loader generation from the current manifest, records the superseded markers, and with `--diff` writes the suggested post-migration rc under `~/.niubash/candidates/`. It never modifies the rc — the removal is always the user's own edit.

Rollback switch: `NIU_PLUGIN_LOADER=off` (`off`/`false`/`0`/`no`) stops the host from loading the generated loader — plugins return to manual-source mode per the documented guidance. The switch only disables loading; it never writes anything, and unsetting it rolls forward.

Control-plane writers are atomic (design §4.4): `save_spec` (`plugins.toml`) and `write_source_registry` (`sources/registry.toml`) swap whole files through a same-dir temp + replace rename, so a concurrent reader never observes a truncate window.

Windows path contract: the bundled WinuxCmd coreutils own the shell tree —
they receive the shell's POSIX spellings verbatim and resolve them in-child —
while every other child, native or a foreign POSIX runtime such as MSYS2 or
Cygwin, always receives native Windows paths, with no per-child probe and no
`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV`-style switch (unixwin/niubash#346). This rides the
WinuxCmd shell-tree layer, so the bundled WinuxCmd pin must be bumped in the
same release.
Windows releases bundle niu-git 2.55.0.5 (`scripts/release/preinstall.json`).
niu-git moves to `layout: flat`: the payload lands under `opt\niugit` and
`mingw64\bin\git.exe` is mapped straight onto `usr\bin\git.exe`, so the `git`
on PATH *is* the git binary — no winuxcmd dispatch hop, no launcher, no MSYS
runtime and no perl in the process tree. `git --version` drops from 72–83 ms
to ~14 ms (Git Bash: 45–103 ms) and `git status` to ~23 ms. Needs WinuxCmd
1.1.9 or newer (the POSIX-unlink hardlink break, unixwin/WinuxCmd#1183);
the release pin already carries 1.1.10.

Shell-face startup is a measured contract (`scripts/perf/shell-face-startup.py`):
execution-level `-c exit` timing for every installed face — the `niu.exe`
payload, the `winuxcmd\bin` / `winuxcmd\usr\bin` `bash.exe`/`sh.exe` links,
and the `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` convention slot — with a
verify-before-record rule (a face that cannot execute prints the failure
note, never a fast number), structural annotations (size, hardlink count,
same-file-as-payload), a `Measure-Command` cross-check mode, and a
deterministic `--check-links` gate: every declared face must be the same
file as the payload `niu.exe`. A measured-time-ratio gate was tried first
and rejected with data — shimmed faces measured 1.04–1.46x the payload
while healthy relinked faces measured 0.91–1.26x, overlapping intervals,
so no ratio separates the states without false kills (niubash#377 CR).
Measured on the 1.4.0

(niubash#376 hygiene): `{app}\winuxcmd\bin` and `{app}\winuxcmd\usr\bin` are
cleared of `*.bak-*` / `*.old-*` / `*.niu-old-*` on install and uninstall —
the same dead-weight class as the existing `niu.exe.old-*` sweep, observed
live as `bash.exe.bak-1.4.0` / `sh.exe.old-shposix` (4 × 226,816 B on real
machines; `*.niu-old-*` covers a relinker crash between park and drop).
Live entry names are never matched. The PATH entry directory contract
(hardlinks only, `usr\bin` off `PATH`, declared entry set) is now documented

The installer's slot contract is pinned by tests, not by a comment
(niubash#398): the ruling that the install tree never claims the
`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` convention slot — the installer runs
`PrivilegesRequired=lowest`, cannot elevate, and the slot directory is

`tests/installer_surface.rs` guards the surface statically: no absolute
foreign path or `Program Files` reference anywhere in `niubash.iss`, every
`[Files]`/`[InstallDelete]`/`[UninstallDelete]`/`[Icons]`/`[Run]` surface
confined to `{app}` and Inno-managed shell folders, `HKCU\Environment\Path`
the only registry value written, and the delete sweeps matched against the
sanctioned retired-shape globs only. `scripts/installer-slot-probe.py` is
the runtime leg: a pure user-directory sandbox replays the executable
installer steps (`--relink-shells`, app-tree teardown) across a full
install/uninstall cycle and asserts the decoy foreign slot — and the real
Git Bash slot, read-only — byte-identical at baseline, after install and
after uninstall, with no face name left outside the removed tree. The same
probe records the niubash#377 quantification: forwarder faces cost one
extra process per `-c` call (chain evidence: 2 processes below the probe,
min ~36 ms) and collapse to the payload itself as hardlinks (1 process,
min ~19 ms, same file as `niu.exe`).
The factory prompt's git segment runs the user's own git instead of the
in-process libgit2 dependency: one bounded
`git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` inside a repository, and no spawn at
all outside one (a few `stat`s, where `__git_ps1` forks anyway). Fidelity
is the reason to switch — sparse checkouts, linked worktrees, submodules and
`safe.directory` refusals are answered by the git the user actually runs
(libgit2 silently dropped the branch segment on old-owner trees once) — and
the cost is unchanged in practice: measured p50 26 ms / max 37 ms per prompt
inside a repository, i.e. the bare git call and nothing more, against Git
Bash's `__git_ps1` 100-300 ms (three to five forks). Isolation rules, one
per incident: never through a shell (a missing git is an OS error, not
`command not found` noise), stdout captured and stderr discarded (git
warnings never reach the screen), `--no-optional-locks` +
`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (never takes `index.lock`), `-c core.fsmonitor=false`
(never starts an fsmonitor daemon from a prompt), a 2 s timeout with the
child killed, and no `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (measured +28 ms per call: it makes
Windows allocate a hidden console for every prompt; a console child inherits
ours and shows no window). This also drops the `git2`/libgit2 dependency:
~1.28 MB of the binary and 323 locked packages (libgit2-sys, url/idna/ICU,
cc, pkg-config, vcpkg, ...). Both niubash#145 startup invariants still pass
(`legacy_niu_plugins_rc_reaches_prompt`,
`legacy_framework_rc_reaches_prompt`): nothing is waited on before the first
paint, and the prompt-scoped child is reaped by the prompt itself. A
brand-new repository (unborn HEAD) now shows its branch, where libgit2's
`head()` errored and the segment vanished.
Fixed: A DSR-silent terminal no longer kills the shell, and TAB completion
commits (unixwin/niubash#373, the #355 follow-up). Interactive startup
used to anchor the prompt with a `ESC[6n` cursor-position query and ABORT
the line editor when it timed out: on a terminal that never answers
(dumb terminals, `script(1)` recordings, some serial/tmux links) every
startup paid a ~2.6 s stall, printed
"niubash: line editor error: The cursor position could not be read within
a normal duration", and exited before painting any prompt. The editor
(reedline 0.50 -> 0.52) now treats the query as advisory — the prompt
paints without a reply and later cycles stay interactive; Windows/ConPTY
is unaffected either way (conhost withholds the client at session attach
until the terminal answers, a terminal-side contract below niu, pinned by
the new `tests/issue373.rs` harness). File completion now commits
like command completion: `cat uniqfi<TAB>` splices the completed word
into the line (the unique match commits outright, the ambiguous set
commits its common prefix and still shows the grid) instead of leaving
the suffix as a menu preview that Enter executed unexpanded — and Enter
submits the line as typed (GNU accept-line), dismissing the grid, where
reedline 0.52's menu would have consumed the first Enter as an
acceptance. The dismissal rides only the completion TAB window: a
Ctrl+R history search's accepting Enter stays the bare event reedline's
search handler implements (a whole `Multiple` batch is dropped there —
unconditionally wrapping it turned the search's Enter into a dead key). Measured TTP on the ConPTY harness is unchanged (niu 3.14 s
vs GNU bash 3.26 s median, transport-floor dominated; internal startup
~70-140 ms — `scripts/perf/ttp-bench.py`).
dirname/basename: slash-shaped operands stay verbatim — `dirname /a/b`
reports `/a` instead of a drive spelling such as `A:`; the slash-drive
argument mask now covers the filesystem-blind string tools
(unixwin/niubash#346).

Changed: The factory default prompt on Windows is now the Git Bash skeleton
(owner adjudication 2026-10-12, #292): green `user@host`, yellow
POSIX-persona cwd, cyan branch (+ dirty `*`) and `$ ` — the MINGW64
environment segment is deliberately omitted (that is MinGW identity,
not this shell's) and there is no static product tag. The branch/dirty
segment reads the repository through git2 (owner-approved library
dependency, Windows-target-only compile) instead of a git child
process, so the prompt path never spawns (the niubash#145 red line):
measured cold 39 ms, warm p50 2.5 ms / p90 3.7 ms per prompt against
Git Bash's per-prompt `__git_ps1` fork (~100-300 ms). Claims still
win: a PS1/theme claim displaces the floor per prompt, and `set -o
vi` keeps its live editing-mode indicator (niubash#184). The skeleton
follows Git Bash's own layout after live owner passes on 2026-10-14:
two rows (info row, then the `$ ` input line on its own row) and the
branch in MINGW64's parentheses — `(master*)`, dirty star inside.
Default TAB completion style is now the multi-per-row grid
(`CompletionStyle::Column`, owner rulings 2026-10-12 + 2026-10-14):
every TAB shows the candidates at once, several per row — the look of a
GNU-style printed listing without the silent first TAB (the literal GNU
readline shape shipped briefly as the default and read as "dead" at the
prompt when TAB #1 had nothing to complete; live owner feedback flipped
it). The literal GNU shape remains an opt-in
(`NIU_COMPLETION_STYLE=gnu` or `niu config set completion.style gnu`):
TAB completes the longest common prefix (a lone candidate completes
outright), and a second TAB on an unchanged line prints the candidates
as width-adaptive columns next to the prompt and repaints it —
implemented as a reedline `Menu` (`completion::gnu_menu`) so it renders
through the normal repaint pipeline. The Ide popup stays opt-in
(`ide`, also accepted: `smart`, `popup`); precedence is env > config
file > default, and `niu doctor` shows the effective style with the
switch commands. The setup wizard gained a completion style step
(current value pre-highlighted) on first run and on `niu setup`
re-runs.
Architecture correction before release: the carapace-bin completion source
merged from #243 is removed from the shell core. No shell hardcodes a
third-party completion provider into its source — the provider belongs in
the rc data layer, integrating through the standard bash completion
protocol the shell already speaks (`complete` compspecs, `NIU_COMPDEFS`
compdef functions, `<cmd>.toml`/`<cmd>.bash` definition files). The native
completion layers are unchanged (embedded WinuxCmd applet TOMLs, bundle
definitions, user completion files); `niu setup` grows an opt-in (default
off) rc snippet for carapace-bin — the same block a bash user writes by
hand, guarded and a no-op until carapace-bin is installed — and a new
docs page documents the rc-based contract for any provider that speaks
the bash completion protocol (carapace is one example). Binary-level tests
pin the rc route: a `complete -W` compspec and a compdef hook sourced from
`~/.niubashrc` both serve Tab candidates, and a standard `.bash` completion
script serves flag candidates through the bash-import channel. Interactive
Tab resolution of `complete -F`/`-C` hook functions remains an engine
(rubash) follow-up, documented in the provider page. Zero compatibility
debt: no 1.4.0 tag ever carried the embedded source, and the `NIU_CARAPACE`
variable was never a released surface (niubash#243, niubash#187).
command-not-found no longer advertises package managers by default
(niubash#249): a typo like `win` prints only the GNU one-liner — the
unsolicited "package search hints" block naming winget/scoop/choco is
removed, and third-party managers are never recommended again. The
recipe/wpm install hints for exact, known tool names (`rg`, `awk`, …)
stay. An opt-in channel returns a wpm-only suggestion:
`niu config set command-not-found-hint wpm` (persisted in the new
`~/.niubash/config.toml`; `NIU_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND_HINT` overrides) — it
suggests one `wpm search --name '<word>'` line only for
high-confidence near-misses (dropping the word's last character hits an
installed command or a known package name), so pure typos stay quiet
even with the switch on. New `niu config get/list/set` subcommand surface
manages the file.

Installer disclosure (niubash#313): the "Create a desktop shortcut"
task is new in 1.4.x and default-checked. Silent installs and upgrades
(`/SILENT`, `/VERYSILENT`) never show the task page, and Inno has no
saved selection for a new task name — so a silent upgrade of a 1.3.x
machine runs the task with its default state and grows a desktop icon
(rewritten in place to the Windows Terminal form by the shortcut step)
without ever asking. Owner ruling: the behavior is intended; it is
disclosed here and in the installer source. Interactive installs keep
remembering an unchecked choice.
Added: Windows Terminal-form desktop/Start-menu shortcuts on Windows 10
(niubash#211, #290): Win10 has no default-terminal setting, so
direct-exe shortcuts used to be hosted by conhost. When a `wt.exe`
resolves (WindowsApps alias -> PATH -> App Paths registry) and the
Niubash WT profile is registered, generated shortcuts take the
`wt.exe -p Niubash` form; without WT the conhost baseline stays
unchanged. `niu --install-wt-shortcuts` (`--update-only`,
`--desktop|--start-menu`) is the standalone verb and the installer
handoff, and it only rewrites links that already exist, so a declined
desktop icon is never grown.
`niu --cwd-state <file>` directory memory for one-shot agent
invocations (#272): opt-in, so a chain of one-shot `niu -c` calls
behaves like one shell — the directory recorded in `<file>` is
restored before startup (before niu's own startup logic, relative
script paths, and `source_non_interactive_env`) and the shell's final
directory is recorded back after every one-shot exit path. Without
the flag, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.
`niu --encoded-command <base64>` (#271): agents and CI callers
get a quoting-free channel — an RFC 4648 payload (padding optional,
ASCII whitespace ignored, must decode to valid UTF-8) executes
through the same one-shot path as `-c`, with the same
`BASH_ENV`/`NIU_ENV` sourcing and `BASH_EXECUTION_STRING` contract.
An optional `v1:` prefix is stripped defensively: MSYS path
conversion rewrites arguments starting with `/`, and a base64 payload
can start with `/`.
Doctor timing advice (niubash#201): `niu doctor` now carries an advisory
row pointing timing/performance-sensitive scripts at the bash 5 builtin
`$EPOCHREALTIME` / `$EPOCHSECONDS` instead of looping on the external
`$(date +%s%N)` — each `date` call pays Windows process creation
(~10-30ms) while the builtin expands in microseconds with the GNU format
`1699999999.123456`. Regression tests pin the format, second-level
agreement with `date +%s`, live monotonic updates, and the speed gap.

niubash#247): `build-android` links aarch64-linux-android and
armv7-linux-androideabi against bionic (NDK r27, API 24) and ships a zip
per leg with ELF-arch verification in place of an on-runner runtime
smoke; `build-openharmony` is check-only for now
(aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos is Tier 2 with host tools — real linking

fetch path yet, so no binary ships from that leg). Both jobs run
continue-on-error and stay out of the release needs, the same incubation
shape the musl leg had before it was tightened; the platform-support

niubash#295, niubash#296). Every git transport a plugin verb spawns —

under a 120 s wall-clock budget (`--timeout <seconds>` on `add`/`sync`,
or `NIU_PLUGIN_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, overrides it per run; the rc

stalled origin costs its own budget and a failed row while the rest of
the spec reconciles. A declaration whose install just failed joins the
stranded population, so `niu plugin sync --prune` removes it in the

for a machine-fed CRLF line break — not by the 50 ms arrival-burst
heuristic. "Text + Enter" in one burst (fast human typing, ConPTY test
drivers, expect scripts, `send-keys`) submits on the first Enter again;
multi-line pastes keep buffering quietly until the user's own Enter
(0 mid-paste executions, niubash#202 contract unchanged). A typeahead
line queued behind a submitting Enter is pushed back and lands, in
order, at the next prompt. The TypeaheadGuard no longer double-injects
swept console input records: the sweeper's self-heal path drains the
buffer before writing it back, so a record can no longer be reinjected
twice (once by the self-heal, once by disarm; niubash#287).

(niubash#308): a paste followed immediately by Enter — one write, the
Enter inside the burst window — used to be swallowed, and a second

chunk-open Enter now runs in the pending branch: silence (or any
other queued key) behind the CR proves the chunk complete, and the

Fixed: Interactive arithmetic corruption (engine rubash 1.3.1): aliases no
longer expand inside compound array assignments. Under oh-my-bash, the
convenience alias `1='cd -'` leaked into the literal
`OMB_VERSINFO=(1 0 0 0 ...)` and corrupted it to
`(_omb_directories_cd - 0 ...)`, killing version arithmetic with
`-: arithmetic syntax error` in interactive sessions (any theme,
powerbash10k included). GNU parity: assignment words are never
alias-expanded (parse.y parse_compound_assignment keeps the whole
`( ... )` in one ASSIGNMENT_WORD token).
Plugin sync state machine: the startup "installed but not declared"
nag now prints only when a spec exists (imperative mode is silent);
`niu plugin sync --adopt` declares installed sources with a
round-trip-stable snapshot (enablement + theme); the setup wizard ends
spec-managed; `niu plugin add` adopts an already-installed source
instead of erroring "remove it first".
No re-download loop: the startup bootstrap memoizes failed installs
(per origin+ref ledger); retries happen only on an explicit
`niu plugin sync`. The bash-it fingerprint now matches the real
upstream layout (its `lib/composure.bash` was removed upstream).
`niu plugin source remove` also drops the spec declaration (no
resurrection), and duplicate spec declarations of one source merge
instead of flipping the rc block every sync.

Added: native path: `/mnt/X/...` operands resolve like `/X/...` and `X:\...` -
the WSL interop spelling (#1172). WSL mounts the Windows drives under
`/mnt`, and that spelling reached argv verbatim whenever a tool was invoked
directly (PowerShell, cmd, a scheduler, an agent) rather than through
rubash, whose argv funnel already pre-translates the form for every child
(rubash#444, rubash#592). `normalize_api_operand_w` now folds `/mnt/X` to
the MSYS `/X` spelling before the drive branch, so a single drive-letter
arm keeps owning every POSIX drive form. The accepted shape matches
rubash's `windows_mnt_drive_argument` byte-for-byte: a lowercase `mnt`
literal, a drive letter of either case, exactly `/mnt/X` or `/mnt/X/...`.
Bare `/mnt` (the WSL root) and non-drive children (`/mnt/data`,
`/mnt/cfoo`, `/mnt/123`) stay verbatim, `/mnt/cygdrive/d` cannot fold
twice, and the existing verbatim classes (`/cygdrive/*`, `/dev/*`, bare
`/`, `/X...` switches) are untouched. Every tool on the shared operand
boundary (ls, du, sed, cp, ...) picks the form up at once; under a
configured shell root the resolution is unchanged, since the niubash#346
shell-ns arm already mapped this exact shape.
wpm: `wpm links verify` reports, by path, every command link that does not
run the installed `winuxcmd.exe` - the diagnosis that was missing while a
stale link could keep one command on an older build for hours without a word.
wpm: `winuxcmd-shim.exe`, a small forwarder behind `layout: shim`
packages. `usr\bin\python.exe` and its siblings used to be a hardlink to an
older `winuxcmd.exe` whose only job was to spawn `opt\<pkg>\<command>.exe`,
so every `python`/`node`/`curl`/`ssh` call paid a whole WinuxCmd startup; the
dispatch hop drops from a measured 24.5 ms to 12.1 ms. An installation without
the forwarder keeps the previous behaviour, and `wpm links rebuild --force`
(which activation already runs) switches existing installs over.
Fixed: wpm: `wpm update winuxcmd` no longer leaves a command link on the previous
image silently. A link that cannot be deleted is parked and replaced, the
failing link is named, the links are verified after the swap and relinked
once, and the detached update helper writes its output to
`.wpm\logs\self-update-<stamp>-<pid>.log` (newest three kept) instead of
discarding it.
wpm: the self-update keeps the newest two rollback copies of
`winuxcmd.exe` and prunes older ones - one machine had accumulated 61.8 MB -
and `wpm clean backup` (and `clean all`) reclaims them.
wpm: a package upgrade now replaces files that a running program holds
open, instead of failing halfway. 1.1.12 refused up front when it *thought* a
destination could not be replaced, but the probe it used — opening the name
with `DELETE` access — succeeds against a file another process has mapped as
its image, while the delete and the overwrite that follow both fail with
Access denied. On a real installation this meant `wpm install niugit --force`
still failed while git's `fsmonitor--daemon` held
`libexec/git-core/git.exe`, and it failed *after* the reconcile and the entry
links had run, leaving the package half-updated.
Destinations are now renamed aside (`<name>.wpm-old-<pid>`) before
anything is written: a rename is exactly what a mapped image permits, the
running process keeps its old bytes, and the operation is reversible. If a
destination cannot even be renamed, the ones already parked are put back and
the install refuses with the culprit and the processes running from it — so
an upgrade is either complete or untouched. Once the install commits, the
parked names are deleted; while the old process still holds them the name
stays, and `wpm clean` removes it later.
wpm: a superseded path the new version no longer maps is parked the same
way instead of aborting the upgrade when a live process holds it.
wpm: `wpm clean staging` and `wpm clean all` also remove parked
`.wpm-old-<pid>` names left by earlier installs.
Verified on a live installation with 28 `fsmonitor--daemon` processes holding
the payload: the forced upgrade succeeds, `usr/bin/git.exe` and `bin/git.exe`
both share the payload inode, and `.wpm/staging` is pruned.
wpm: an install is refused up front when a destination is held open by
a running program, instead of failing halfway through. A file held by another
process cannot be replaced on Windows at all — delete and overwrite both
return *Access denied* — so the old behaviour could leave a package
half-updated; an upgrade of niugit was observed with `opt/niugit` on the new
version while the PATH entry still ran the old one. WPM now probes every
destination before writing anything, lists the files and the programs running
from them, and leaves the installation exactly as it was. Close the listed
programs and retry.
wpm: flat-layout file mappings are copied from the package's payload
rather than the extraction directory, so a mapping that duplicates a path
already covered by a directory mapping no longer produces a second copy of
the package and a PATH entry pointing into `.wpm/staging` (the two
destinations now share one inode). The staging tree is pruned after a
successful install.
Added: wpm: every package command gets a PATH entry link at
`<root>/bin/<cmd>.exe` — a hardlink to the real binary (the payload under
`opt/<pkg>/` for shim packages, the mapped binary in `usr/bin/` for flat
ones), never a launcher, so nothing extra runs per invocation. The links are
recorded in the package receipt and kept in sync by install, update,
`wpm links rebuild` and uninstall.

Fixed: wpm: `wpm update winuxcmd` swaps the image by unlinking the old name
and moving the staged binary into place instead of overwriting a
running/mapped image in place. The in-place write fails with "being used by
another process" whenever any process holds the file (observed on a live
install, where the update silently kept the old version), and writing under
a mapped image is unsafe for the processes already running from it. The
in-place path remains the fallback when the unlink itself fails.
wpm: installing a package reconciles its own previous install first -
destinations the new artifact no longer maps are removed and, on a version
change, files inside still-mapped directories that the new payload dropped
are pruned. Before, a layout change left inert leftovers behind (the retired
shim launcher `opt\<pkg>\<cmd>.exe` after a move to `layout: flat`, or a
stale DLL in a PATH directory from older flat packaging). Only paths
recorded in the package's own receipt are touched, they must resolve inside
the root, and the winuxcmd image and the running executable are never
deleted.
wpm: `outdated` orders versions instead of comparing strings, so a stale
mirror advertising an older version no longer reports a
`update available: 2.55.0.5 -> 2.55.0.4` downgrade. The order is the
dotted-numeric core plus, when present, a Debian-style packaging revision
(`5.4.1-unixwin2` > `5.4.1-unixwin1` > `5.4.1`) - what a repackaged artifact
needs, since the upstream version stays and our rebuild gets a revision.
Vendor spellings (`9.5.0.0p1`, `r42`, ...) keep the conservative "any
difference is an update" rule.

Added: native_path: normalized API operands now resolve the shell tree — the bare
`/` and every path below the configured install root, `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`,
`/home` and the `/mnt/X` WSL drive form — and a shell-namespaced operand's
canonical result is re-expressed in the POSIX face, so `readlink -f` and
`realpath` agree with `pwd`. The executable-leaf open order (an existing
as-spelled path wins, else the `X.exe` sibling) keeps `test -f /usr/bin/seq`
and `head -1 /usr/bin/seq` consistent while `ls -d` keeps the operand
spelling. The layer is inert unless a shell root is configured, so standalone
WinuxCmd keeps its native dialect (unixwin/niubash#346).

Fixed: wpm: installing a payload file over an existing `usr\bin` command name
now breaks the old WinuxCmd multicall hardlink with POSIX-semantics unlink
instead of a plain `DeleteFileW`. Every `usr\bin` entry is a link to the
same on-disk image as the running `wpm.exe`/`winuxcmd.exe`, so the plain
delete self-locked and failed with `Access denied` ("failed to break
WinuxCmd hardlink"). Only `layout: flat` packages, whose payload maps the
real binary onto `usr\bin\<cmd>.exe`, ever reach this path — first hit by
`wpm install niugit --force` (unixwin/niu-git#8). The same POSIX unlink is
now used by the stale-link cleanup and alias-replacement paths, which had
the identical hazard.

Changed: wpm: shim payload resolution checks shallow per-package locations
(`<pkg>/<cmd>.exe`, plus `bin/`, `libexec/`, `lib/`, `sbin/`, `usr/bin/` at
depth 1-3, shallowest wins) before falling back to the bounded recursive
scan, so command-differs-from-package shims (`git` -> `niugit`, `cargo` ->
`rust`, `clang` -> `llvm`, `nu` -> `nushell`, `nvim` -> `neovim`) no longer
pay a whole-`opt/` tree walk on every invocation (~15k files). `time git`
through the shim 212 ms -> 77 ms; a prompt-style git hook batch
847 ms -> 291 ms; direct-hit shims (`python`, `curl`, `node`) are unchanged
(unixwin/niu-git#8).
Fixed: ls: `/` (also spelled `//`, `///`) resolves to the shell root named by
`__RUBASH_SHELL_ROOT`/`NIU_ROOT`/`WINUXSH_ROOT`/`RUBASH_ROOT` instead of
enumerating the drive root, independently of the current directory;
recursive listings keep the logical `/...` headers while lookups and entry
metadata go through the shell root (unixwin/niubash#346).

Added: diff3: full GNU diffutils 3.10 alignment on the shared diff engine —
three-way block merge (`make_3way_diff`), default report with GNU's
odd-one-out section rules, ed scripts (`-A`/`-e`/`-E`/`-3`/`-x`/`-X` with
`-i` final write), merged output (`-m`, `-L` labels, `-T` initial tab,
`--strip-trailing-cr`, `--diff-program`), `-` stdin operands and GNU exit
statuses (0 ok / 1 conflicts / 2 trouble) with byte-verified usage
diagnostics (issue #1127, P1).
sdiff: rebuilt on `diff --side-by-side` output — GNU's gutter formula,
`|`/`<`/`>`/`(`/`)` row markers and `/`/`\` separators for rows missing a
trailing newline; `-l`/`-s`, `-w`/`--tabsize`/`-t`, the ignore-option
family (`-i`/`-E`/`-Z`/`-b`/`-W`/`-B`/`-I`/`-a`/`--strip-trailing-cr`,
`-d`/`-H`/`--diff-program`) forwarded into matching only, and `-o` merged
output that auto-merges non-interactively (overlaps keep the left column)
per issue #1127, P1.
Changed: winuxcmd: the bare `winuxcmd` listing groups commands into GNU
coreutils-style sections (File operations, Text processing, Shell
utilities, ...) with alphabetical entries and a discovery guide
(`winuxcmd <command> --help`, `winuxcmd help <command>`,
`winuxcmd --list-all`, `wpm search`); `winuxcmd --list-all` preserves the
flat alphabetical listing. When the system locale is non-English and its
i18n catalog is not installed, one hint line points at the matching WPM
package (`wpm install winuxcmd-i18n-zh-cn` + `WINUX_LANG`) (#1155).
seq: output is assembled into 64 KiB buffer chunks instead of one
`WriteFile` per line, and integral first/increment sequences (default
fixed format, precision 0, no `--format`/`-w`, |operands| <= 2^52) emit
through a `std::to_chars` fast path like GNU seq.c's integer bypass.
100k lines, release build: `seq 1 100000` 332 ms -> ~45 ms and
`seq 1 100000 | wc -l` 903 ms -> ~45 ms (GNU/WSL oracle 7-10 ms; the
residual is Windows process spawn). The byte stream is unchanged — a
regression test pins all 588,895 bytes across several flush rounds
diff: side-by-side output now shares the GNU diffutils `side.c`
printer with sdiff (identical rows, `(`/`)` remainders, `/`/`\`
separators, common rows for equal inputs); `-E` expands tabs across the
whole line for matching, `-B`/`-I` drop ignored hunks and realign their
lines positionally instead of filtering buffers, and a final line without
a newline only compares equal to the other side's incomplete last line
docs: the GNU coreutils compatibility records the one deliberate
Windows deviation around literal-glob operands — NTFS/Win32 forbid `*` in
file names, so `touch 'x*x'` reports the NTFS error where GNU creates the
literal file, `touch -c 'x*x'` silently skips like GNU (fixed in #1152),
and the derived `ls 'x*x'` miss is a consequence of GNU's own creation
succeeding; the touch test exemption is registered in
`DOCS/gnu-coreutils/touch.md` and `COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md` (#1143, #1167).
Fixed: spawn: every child-process launch (the xargs/`find -exec`/pipeline
spawn family) resolves through a shared GNU `execvp`-style resolver —
bare names search PATH only (no cwd or implicit System32 shadowing, so
`sort`/`find`/`tree`... pick the GNU-compatible binary the caller put on
PATH first) and POSIX PATH spellings (`/c/...`, `/cygdrive/c/...`,
`:`-separated entries) are split and converted before resolution
(owner-reported, #1169).
find: POSIX drive-form start points (`/c/...`, `/d/...`,
`/cygdrive/c/...`) now resolve through the same operand boundary as every
other tool's path operands, matching msys find semantics where the tool's
own POSIX layer handles the start point. Command-line roots, `-files0-from`
entries, and the `-files0-from` source operand all go through it (#1170).
tests: the grep junction recursion cases degrade to a SKIP on hosts
without symlink-creation privilege (error 1314) instead of failing, mirroring
the `*_or_skip` helper every other unit test file uses (#1168). New tput
GNU-differential tests pin that every tput path — success, unknown
capability, missing operand — leaves piped stdin untouched, the contract
GNU tput is known for (#1166).
i18n: the WPM message catalog resolves at the WinuxCmd install root, so
localized messages work when `winuxcmd.exe` is invoked through a shim or
PATH entry outside the install directory (#1151).
touch: GNU-parity handling of unmatched literal-glob operands — names
that glob to nothing are treated as missing under `-c` (skipped) instead of
being created verbatim, matching GNU coreutils (#1152).
wpm: interaction-audit fixes (#1156). `wpm outdated` now anchors
installed versions on install receipts, so it keeps reporting a pending
update after `wpm index update` instead of flipping to "all up to date"
while old files are still on disk. `wpm install --json` prints one
machine-readable payload (statuses `installed`, `already_installed`,
`would_install`, `not_found`, `not_installable`, `preflight_failed`,
`download_failed`, `error`) with all human progress routed to stderr, and
`wpm index update --json` prints a matching payload. `wpm --help` now
documents the `install` `--force` reinstall/overwrite semantics. Verified
by measurement: piped `y`/`n` confirmation on `wpm uninstall` stdin (and
`-y` in any argument position) already behaved correctly on this branch,
and locked destination files already fail loudly with exit 1 on both
install and uninstall; regression tests pin all of these behaviors.
du: an operand's trailing separator run collapses to a single slash —
`du src/` prints `src/` and `src/bin` (never `src//bin`), `du src//` prints
byte-identically to `du src/`, and `du src` keeps the plain form, matching
GNU coreutils (#1159).
du, sed: POSIX drive-form operands (`/d/...`, `/cygdrive/d/...`)
resolve through the shared operand boundary — du used to reject them
with ENOENT while accepting `D:/...`, and sed could not read them as
input files, `-i` targets, `-f` script files or the `r`/`w`/`W`
script-embedded paths. Both now route operands through the same
boundary grep/wc/head/find already use (the L2 self-parse contract,
uniformly applied); error messages and the `=`/`F` filename display
keep the operand text as typed (#1174).
wpm: candidate index sources are the built-in registry plus
`user_sources` only — a `sources` array declared inside the cached index
file is no longer merged, so one poisoned fetch can no longer persistently
inject new download locations; `wpm index update` now records the winning
source (`last_success_source`) and the SHA-256 of the persisted index
(`last_index_sha256`) and warns when the index content changes while being
served from a non-preferred source; the `wpm index update --json` payload
carries `index_sha256` (#1176).
wpm: the loopback proxy fallback (probing `127.0.0.1:7897/7890/7891/
7892/7893/10808/10809` after direct failures) is off by default; any
unprivileged local process could otherwise listen there and serve both
index and artifacts past the index's own sha256 checks. Opt in via
`allow_loopback_fallback: true` in `.wpm/config.json`, or configure a
trusted proxy with `--proxy`/environment variables (#1177).

Fixed — upstream lane wt50 (2026-10-03): yes: a broken-pipe write death now reports exit status 141 (the
SIGPIPE emulation other streaming tools use) instead of exit 1, so
`yes | head -n 3` shows 141 on the producer side exactly like GNU
coreutils (#1142). Non-pipe write errors keep the fatal exit-1 path.
Fixed — upstream lane wt48 (2026-10-03): cp: every stat/open route now goes through the shared API-path
boundary (`native_path::make_api_path_operand`, the mv/install
invariant), so POSIX-drive-form operands (`/d/x`, `/cygdrive/d/x`) work
in any combination with Windows-form operands instead of failing
`cannot stat ... No such file or directory` at the source-existence,
destination-directory, `-t`, same-file, symlink, and recursive-child
gates (#1145, unixwin/niubash#124 Option B). `cp -s` stores the
dialect-resolved source spelling as link text (a typed `/d/x` link text
can never resolve on native Windows).
ls: file operands and `-d` directory operands resolve POSIX drive
forms — `std::filesystem::absolute` used to fold `/d/x` against the
current drive root (`D:\d\x`) before the boundary could convert it
(#1145). A bare root operand (`ls /`, `ls -d /`, `ls //`) lists the
current drive root (the platform's `/` mapping, consistent with
`cygpath -w /`): the `\\?\` spelling of a drive root is rejected by
attribute probes, and the root/`\*` enumeration pattern is now built
with a path-aware join (`GetFullPathNameW` mis-parses the concatenated
native_path (shared boundary): `normalize_api_operand_w` folds the
Cygwin drive prefix (`/cygdrive/d/x`, both separators) into the MSYS
spelling before drive-letter conversion, giving every command that
already routes through the boundary (cat, cp, install, mv, ...) cygdrive
support uniformly; `to_extended_path` keeps bare drive roots un-prefixed
and folds separators before `GetFullPathNameW` (#1145).
Fixed — upstream lane wt41 (2026-10-02): mv: operands in MSYS drive form (`/d/x`) are routed through the
shared API-path boundary like cp/install, so mixing Windows-form and
POSIX-form operands in one invocation works in any combination (#1140,
unixwin/niubash#124); GNU coreutils under MSYS accepts either dialect.
The copy fallback also no longer mislabels regular files as directories,
actually moves directories across volumes (they used to report success
while doing nothing), refuses to move a directory into itself
(`cannot copy a directory, X, into itself, Y`, GNU copy.c:2091), and
honors a trailing separator on DEST (`failed to access 'DEST': Not a
directory` instead of silently creating/overwriting the stripped name).
mktemp: the printed name keeps the `-p`/`--tmpdir` operand's dialect
(`-p /d/...` echoes `/d/.../x.XXXXXX`, `-p /cygdrive/d/...` likewise),
so shell round-trips that capture the output stay self-consistent with
POSIX-form variables (#1141); Windows-form operands and the TMPDIR/
default-temp paths keep the native display form.
xargs: option parsing stops at the utility name; every argument
after it is passed to the utility verbatim (POSIX xargs operand
semantics, GNU findutils) — `xargs cat -n` no longer errors on `-n`,
`xargs wc -l` no longer silently consumes `-l` as `--max-lines`, and
`xargs echo -- help` keeps the `--` (#1139).
